capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Cars.com (VW release): 35.8 kWh, up from 24.2 kWh (2017-2020).

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: German Wikipedia: net 31.5 kWh per the registration table (2017-2020).

chemistry.notes: Estimated: EV Database NZ lists the e-Golf (used examples 2017-2021) with battery type NMC, 32 kWh usable, 400 V, DC 40 kW. Community database, not a VW statement. The 24.2 kWh 2015-2016 pack is not covered by that page.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: 323 V nominal is stated for the 24.2 kWh pack (German Wikipedia); no voltage is given for the 35.8 kWh pack, which has the same cell architecture family; 400 V class either way.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: VW's first automatic battery preconditioning arrived with the 2024 ID.4 software (InsideEVs: ID.4/ID.5 built 2020-2024 lacked it, automatic from 2024); the e-Golf (2015-2020) predates it and no e-Golf page describes a battery-warming feature (Wikipedia mentions only a heat pump option and Eco+ mode).

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: same 40 kW CCS ceiling carried to the 35.8 kWh 2017-2020 car; VW says 80 % in about an hour (Cars.com 2017); no 2017+ page states kW.

ac_max_kw.notes: Cars.com (VW release): "Newly standard is a 7.2-kW onboard charger" (2017). 2018-2020 compared: no change shown. Canada not separately sourced.
